definitions.terms: In every test a character is one UTF-16 unit of the JavaScript string (every route here holds only characters of 16 bits). The text is the whole route text as it stands, the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def. Nothing is trimmed. The text before the mark is every character from the start of the text up to, and not including, the mark; the text after the mark is every character after it to the end. A letter is any character the JavaScript test \p{L} with the u flag matches; whitespace is what \s matches. The word before the mark is the longest run of letters that ends directly before the mark (empty if the character before it is not a letter); the word after the mark is the longest run of letters that begins after the mark once any whitespace directly after it is passed over (empty if the next character is not a letter). What the bracket holds means the characters between that opener and its closer: the template's c.group. Contains a semicolon means the semicolon character stands anywhere in the text before the mark. Is one of the strings in a list means is equal to one string of that list, character for character and whole. Every string and every list minds case. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence. Each mark here has one shape, so every occurrence of a mark takes that mark's shape; the tests are stated all the same, and each holds for every occurrence.
